bull_bear.body: Diligent product-wise ROI monitoring before launch; Funding multi-category expansion while protecting returns; Strategic JV with Hisense to share capex burden for new facilities.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity price volatility (copper, aluminum) exceeding pass-through capabilities; Seasonal demand mismatch for AC; High channel inventory (4-4.5 Mn units) delaying order normalization; Regulatory costs (E-waste, BEE norms) squeezing brand budgets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'resilience' despite external headwinds; Clear strategic shift from volume-only RAC to balanced high-margin mix; Transparent on cost pass-through mechanics.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Trade payable days dropped drastically in Q3 due to consumption of existing inventory without new procurement (seasonal lull); Normalized payable days are 90-100. Management explicitly states top-2 customer concentration (now 35-40%) is 'ideal' and will not be reduced further, shifting focus to wallet-share expansion via cross-selling rather than dilution.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Rs 4,700 Mn capex programme is described as "largely funded".
- Leverage stepped up in FY26: gross debt Rs 7,070 Mn (FY25 Rs 3,697 Mn), net debt Rs 6,912 Mn (FY25 Rs 3,555 Mn), net debt/equity 0.72x (FY25 0.37x), against net worth of Rs 9,603 Mn.
- Returns compressed on the enlarged base: RoCE 5.2% in FY26 vs 10.8% in FY25; RoE 0.4% vs 6.0%.
- Working capital absorbed cash: inventory days 161 (FY25: 98), receivable days 68 (50), payable days 138 (91) and cash conversion cycle 91 days (57); net fixed asset turns fell to 2.4x from 3.2x.
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026: promoters 46.4%, public 34.9%, DII 11.3%, FPI 7.4% — the deck reads promoter holding as "continued alignment" and "institutional ownership (DII + FPI = ~19%)" as "a stable base".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Highest level of backward integration for RACs at a single location in India - stated as a key competitive advantage enabling superior cost management, efficient inventory control and reduced exposure to supply chain volatility, particularly from imports
- Second-largest RAC ODM in India by volume of units manufactured, with a legacy spanning over two decades as a manufacturing partner to prominent Indian and global brands
- In-house manufacture of critical components - heat exchangers, PCBAs, copper tubing, cross flow fans, universal motors, induction coils, sheet metal and injection-moulded parts - for both captive consumption and external supply
- Dedicated R&D centres at Bhiwadi, Dehradun and Sri City with advanced testing and design facilities including NABL-accredited labs
- Multi-site manufacturing footprint across Dehradun, Bhiwadi and Sri City facilitating efficient pan-India logistics and proximity to key customer markets
- Quality system spanning Incoming (IQC), Line (LQC) and Outgoing (OQC) quality control plus early-life and reliability testing, backed by ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certification
- Access to government incentive schemes - PLI for White Goods, RIPS 2024 in Rajasthan with Large Category status under the ESDM thrust sector, and ECMS under MeitY
- SAP S/4 HANA implemented to optimise operations and guarantee accurate record maintenance
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Qualified audit opinion on recoverability of disputed trade receivables — The statutory auditor issued a Qualified Opinion on the FY 2025-26 standalone financial statements: trade receivables include a disputed balance which the Company believes has a high probability of recovery and against which no provision has been recognised. With the matter under legal dispute and in the absence of sufficient appropriate evidence on the customer's ability to pay, the auditor was unable to determine whether any adjustment is required to the carrying amount of trade receivables, to the expected credit loss allowance under Ind AS 109, or to profit and equity.
- RAC demand cyclicality, weather dependence and channel-inventory build — The Room Air Conditioner business witnessed temporary softness in FY 2025-26 owing to multiple short-term factors, and the Board's report attributes the elongation of working capital to elevated channel inventory across the industry and a demand deferral cycle that affected the broader FMCD sector - a seasonal, single-season-weighted demand profile the Company does not control.
- Working-capital elongation and rising leverage — Working capital days moved to 91 days in FY26 from 57 days in FY25 and the net debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.72x in FY26 as compared to 0.37x in FY25, described as calibrated borrowings to support capacity and working capital requirements; the combination raises funding cost and balance-sheet sensitivity if the demand recovery is delayed.
- Margin compression from industry-wide headwinds — EBITDA margins stood at 6.01% in FY26 as against 7.26% in FY25, which management attributes to industry-wide headwinds rather than any structural weakness in operations; as an ODM the ability to hold margin depends on passing cost movements through to brand customers.
- Geopolitical, energy-price and supply-chain exposure on input costs — Ongoing geopolitical tensions including conflicts in the Middle East kept uncertainty elevated, leading to supply chain and trade disruptions, increasing volatility in energy markets and a rise in critical input prices; the MD&A adds that disruptions across key shipping routes and volatility in crude oil and commodity prices led to higher procurement and freight costs, periodic disruptions in material availability and longer lead times.
- Climate transition and carbon-regulation compliance risk — BRSR material issue 1, GHG Emissions and Climate Change Mitigation, flagged as a Risk: increasing climate-related regulations, carbon pricing mechanisms, customer expectations and transition risks may expose the Company to higher compliance costs, operational disruptions and reputational risks, with increased capital expenditure for energy-efficient technologies and renewable energy projects.
- Physical climate risk to manufacturing and logistics continuity — BRSR material issue 2, Climate Change Adaptation, flagged as a Risk: extreme weather events, changing climatic conditions and resource constraints may disrupt manufacturing operations, logistics and the availability of critical inputs, with financial impact from production downtime, logistics and raw-material supply disruption and reduced manufacturing capacity utilisation.
- Waste and circularity compliance alongside shifting product-efficiency regulation — BRSR material issue 4, Waste Management and Circularity, warns that inadequate management of metal scrap, plastic waste, packaging waste and other industrial solid waste may result in regulatory non-compliance, increased disposal costs and environmental impacts; the MD&A separately notes enhanced BEE energy-efficiency standards and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations reshaping product design and reverse-logistics requirements across the industry.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: RAC: Marginal 1% YoY decline (industry degrowth); SDA: +30% YoY (Air fryers, nutri blenders); LDA: +74% YoY (Washing machines, coolers); Components: +61% YoY (PCBs, copper parts, plastic molding for AC, meters, coolers). RAC contribution ~57-60%, targeting 55% by FY28/29.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Self-described as "Leading RAC ODM", "Largest Induction Cooktop ODM/OEM" and "Leading Air-Fryer ODM", with a diversified portfolio spanning RAC, LDA, SDA and Components.
- Scale markers on the 'at a glance' page: Total Income FY26 of Rs 19,107 Mn, 72+ trusted customers, 19 product categories, 5 manufacturing locations, 3 NABL-certified R&D labs and '2 decades+' industry experience.
- Stated ambition to "Position EPACK as a strategic single-source manufacturing partner across multiple product categories, enabling deeper customer integration and long-term business partnerships."
- Customer de-risking: top-2 customer concentration fell from 72% of revenue in FY23 to 38%, which the deck calls "materially de-risking the revenue base" (FY26 read 37%; the deck attributes the Q1 FY27 uptick to the RAC-heavy seasonal quarter).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [PLI] The Company has not accrued any PLI income during Q1 FY27, whereas it had accrued PLI income of Rs 133 Mn during Q1 FY26 — the deck footnotes this against its revenue, EBITDA and PBT figures.
- [JV] EPAVO (Bhiwadi) is a JV within the five-plant footprint; the consolidated share of JV loss widened each year — Rs (8) Mn FY23, Rs (15) Mn FY24, Rs (30) Mn FY25, Rs (65) Mn FY26.
- [Margin narrative] The deck frames the current margin pressure as "a sector-wide theme this quarter" and sets the near-term priority as "translating record scale into profitability".
- [Market] Stock data as on 30 June 2026: CMP Rs 230.81, 52-week high/low Rs 414.7 / 196.0, market cap Rs 22,210 Mn, 96 Mn shares outstanding, average volume 1,841k; the deck says the stock "underperformed the Sensex over FY26, tracking the earnings pressure across the RAC sector - a re-rating opportunity if margins and returns recover."
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: EPACK Durable designs and manufactures room air conditioners (split indoor units, outdoor units and window air conditioners), large and small domestic appliances and critical components for prominent Indian and global consumer-appliance brands, providing end-to-end product solutions from design and development through manufacturing and supply chain management. The business is structured around three expanding product verticals - RACs, LDAs and SDAs - supported by in-house component manufacturing for both captive consumption and external supply. Manufacturing runs from Dehradun (Uttarakhand), Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) and Sri City (Andhra Pradesh), backed by dedicated R&D centres at all three locations.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Room Air Conditioners (RACs):** Split AC Indoor Units (IDUs), Outdoor Units (ODUs), Window Air Conditioners (WACs)
- **Large Domestic Appliances (LDAs):** Air coolers, Washing machines
- **Small Domestic Appliances (SDAs):** Induction cooktops, Infrared cooktop, Mixer grinders, Water dispensers, Air fryers, Nutri Blenders, Vacuum Cleaner, Tower Fan
- **Components:** Heat exchangers, Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBAs), Copper tubing, Cross Flow Fan, Induction Coil, Universal Motor, Plastic moulding, Sheet metal parts, BLDC Motors for Room Air Conditioners, BLDC Kits, HVLS Fans
- **Upcoming products:** Coffee Maker, Hair Dryer, Air Purifier
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:

- Bumjin India Audio Products Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly Owned Subsidiary, 100% held; incorporated on June 27, 2025 during FY 2025-26.

July 22, 2022 and the joint venture w.e.f. closing business hours of September 30, 2024, after the stake rose from 26% to 50% through a rights issue; accounted for using the equity method.
- Sri City Electronics Manufacturing Cluster Private Limited — related party: The Company's note states these are NOT related parties as per Ind AS 24 - it is a Special Purpose Vehicle whose non-transferable shares are held under MeitY guidelines for the lease of land under the Electronics Manufacturing Cluster project at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh. The Company held 41.85% of its equity share capital at March 31, 2025 and transferred 12,26,472 excess shares during FY 2025-26 to comply with the MeitY 25% cap. Listed here only because the relation vocabulary has no SPV-investment option; no financials reproduced.

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margins: RAC ~14-15%; SDA/LDA/Components ~16-18%. Cost Headwinds: 8-10% price hike required (50% BEE re-rating, 50% commodity lag from Oct-Dec); Commodity pass-through mechanism protects absolute margins but may compress % margins if base prices rise significantly.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: AC segment 25-30% CAGR to 2030; Industry AC growth 15-20% in CY26; Margin: Targeting 7.5-8% EBITDA medium-term; Order Inflow: Strong RFQs for new BEE-rated products; Capex: INR 450 Cr planned over 12-18 months (INR 218 Cr spent in 9M FY26, INR 225 Cr remaining).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Described as 'very robust' with brands planning 15-20% growth over FY25 numbers; Current production ramping for new BEE-rated units; Inventory liquidation of old-rated stock (4-4.5 Mn units in channel) expected to normalize by end-Q4 FY26, triggering fresh manufacturing orders.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Washing machine vertical (fully auto top/front load) ramping with new MNC customers; Hisense JV commencing production Q4 FY26 (RAC, then WM/TV); Component segment expanding beyond AC to electrical meters and audio; New SDA launches (vacuum cleaners, tower fans) in Q4 FY26.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Diversify beyond the seasonal RAC business by scaling the Small Domestic Appliances, Large Domestic Appliances and Components verticals - FY 2026-27 focus is on strengthening the core RAC business while accelerating scale-up of SDA and LDA through new product development, deeper customer engagement and a healthy order pipeline.
- Deepen and broaden the customer base: deeper penetration across key customer accounts plus new relationships took the customer base from 55 in FY 2024-25 to 72 in FY 2025-26, with continued expansion of market presence targeted.
- Increase localisation and backward integration of components, strengthening the component ecosystem to improve cost, lead times and value addition.
- Expand the manufacturing footprint to five facilities - the dedicated Sri City plant under the Hisense partnership commenced operations through wholly-owned subsidiary EMTPL in Q4 FY 2025-26 and the EPAVO greenfield facility at Bhiwadi was completed with trial production commenced.
- Enter adjacent categories and build new growth platforms that enhance revenues and margins - diversification into the energy meter component segment and entry into smart audio products through the Bumjin Electronics partnership.
- Drive higher utilisation across existing and recently commissioned capacities through disciplined execution and stronger operational efficiencies.
- Leverage government manufacturing schemes - participation in the PLI scheme for the RAC and Components business, approval and Entitlement Certificates under RIPS 2024 for Bhiwadi, and participation in the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS).
- Use R&D-led innovation to advance a pipeline of higher-margin products across RAC, SDA and LDA, including fully automatic top-loading washing machines, tower fans, energy-efficient induction cooktops, hair dryers, air purifiers and coffee makers.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was an expansion year: the Company invested a total CAPEX of Rs 2,971 million directed at localisation, backward integration of component capabilities and future capacity expansion, against a Strategic CAPEX Roadmap with a total investment outlay of Rs 4,700 million spread across the Dehradun, Bhiwadi and Sri City facilities of EPACK Durable and the EMTPL facility at Sri City. Operations commenced under the Hisense partnership through wholly-owned subsidiary EPACK Manufacturing Technologies Private Limited (EMTPL) at Sri City in Q4 FY 2025-26, and EMTPL is expected to gradually contribute to revenues, product mix and future growth as operations scale over the coming quarters. Targeted capital expenditure continues to be deployed to ramp up capacity at newer facilities like Sri City and to support new product lines such as washing machines, while component capability is being widened including a joint venture to produce BLDC motors. Going forward, management says the focus remains on disciplined scale-up and optimising capacity utilisation to realise the full potential of these investments; Phase-2 investment opportunities under RIPS 2024 at Bhiwadi are under evaluation with a focus on advanced RAC components, electronics manufacturing, localisation and export-oriented production. Alongside plant capex, an aggregate solar power generation capacity of 2,332 kW has been installed across all manufacturing units and in-house nitrogen generation plants were established at the Sri City, Bhiwadi and Dehradun facilities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Household RAC penetration in India remains at around 8-10%, significantly below other Asian markets, giving substantial headroom for growth alongside rising temperatures, frequent heatwaves and increasing affordability.
- India's air conditioning market, valued at approximately USD 4.46 billion in 2025, is projected to grow at a CAGR of 14.53% through 2034, underscoring the opportunity for organised manufacturers.
- India's consumer durables market is projected to reach approximately Rs 5.39 lakh crore by FY 2029-30, registering a CAGR of around 14%.
- Management expects improved customer demand conditions and gradual normalisation in industry inventory levels, supported by favourable domestic factors and supportive policy measures.
- Non-RAC segments are the growth engine: SDA and LDA grew on healthy order inflows from existing and newly launched products, while enhanced localisation and deeper customer integration drove strong growth in the Components division.
- FY 2025-26 was a challenging year for the RAC industry - unseasonal weather, inventory correction across channels and revised BEE norms hit industry demand and profitability, a transition-year effect rather than a structural one in management's framing.
- Margin narrative: EBITDA margin of 6.01% absorbed a one-time reversal of previously recognised PLI income accrued April to December 2025, partly mitigated by RIPS 2024 incentive income recognised in Q4, of which part related to earlier periods.
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP is projected to grow between 6.8% and 7.2% in FY 2026-27, with consumer demand expected to remain resilient on rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and premiumisation.
- Structural demand shifts: premiumisation, energy efficiency and BEE labelling, AI/IoT-enabled smart appliances, Tier II and Tier III penetration, omnichannel and e-commerce expansion, and EPR-driven circularity.
- Diversification of global supply chains is expected to create opportunities for India to strengthen its position as a manufacturing and export hub for consumer durables and electronics.
- SDA and LDA growth was driven by healthy order inflows from both existing and newly launched products (no quantified order book disclosed).
- FY 2026-27 scale-up of SDA and LDA is to be supported by new product development, deeper customer engagement and a healthy order pipeline.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: EPACK delivered resilient Q3 growth (13.5% YoY) with margin expansion (7.41%) driven by a 74% surge in LDA and 61% in Components, successfully offsetting a marginal RAC decline. The strategic pivot away from RAC dependency (now ~57-60%) toward higher-margin SDA, LDA, and components is de-risking the model ahead of a projected 15-20% industry recovery in CY26 driven by new BEE norms.

currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was an expansion year: the Company invested a total CAPEX of Rs 2,971 million directed at localisation, backward integration of component capabilities and future capacity expansion, against a Strategic CAPEX Roadmap with a total investment outlay of Rs 4,700 million spread across the Dehradun, Bhiwadi and Sri City facilities of EPACK Durable and the EMTPL facility at Sri City. Targeted capital expenditure continues to be deployed to ramp up capacity at newer facilities like Sri City and to support new product lines such as washing machines, while component capability is being widened including a joint venture to produce BLDC motors. Alongside plant capex, an aggregate solar power generation capacity of 2,332 kW has been installed across all manufacturing units and in-house nitrogen generation plants were established at the Sri City, Bhiwadi and Dehradun facilities.

risks.risk: Qualified audit opinion on recoverability of disputed trade receivables
risks.note: The statutory auditor issued a Qualified Opinion on the FY 2025-26 standalone financial statements: trade receivables include a disputed balance which the Company believes has a high probability of recovery and against which no provision has been recognised. With the matter under legal dispute and in the absence of sufficient appropriate evidence on the customer's ability to pay, the auditor was unable to determine whether any adjustment is required to the carrying amount of trade receivables, to the expected credit loss allowance under Ind AS 109, or to profit and equity.

risks.risk: RAC demand cyclicality, weather dependence and channel-inventory build
risks.note: The Room Air Conditioner business witnessed temporary softness in FY 2025-26 owing to multiple short-term factors, and the Board's report attributes the elongation of working capital to elevated channel inventory across the industry and a demand deferral cycle that affected the broader FMCD sector - a seasonal, single-season-weighted demand profile the Company does not control.

Working capital days moved to 91 days in FY26 from 57 days in FY25 and the net debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.72x in FY26 as compared to 0.37x in FY25, described as calibrated borrowings to support capacity and working capital requirements; the combination raises funding cost and balance-sheet sensitivity if the demand recovery is delayed.

EBITDA margins stood at 6.01% in FY26 as against 7.26% in FY25, which management attributes to industry-wide headwinds rather than any structural weakness in operations; as an ODM the ability to hold margin depends on passing cost movements through to brand customers.

risks.risk: Geopolitical, energy-price and supply-chain exposure on input costs
risks.note: Ongoing geopolitical tensions including conflicts in the Middle East kept uncertainty elevated, leading to supply chain and trade disruptions, increasing volatility in energy markets and a rise in critical input prices; the MD&A adds that disruptions across key shipping routes and volatility in crude oil and commodity prices led to higher procurement and freight costs, periodic disruptions in material availability and longer lead times.

risks.risk: Climate transition and carbon-regulation compliance risk
risks.note: BRSR material issue 1, GHG Emissions and Climate Change Mitigation, flagged as a Risk: increasing climate-related regulations, carbon pricing mechanisms, customer expectations and transition risks may expose the Company to higher compliance costs, operational disruptions and reputational risks, with increased capital expenditure for energy-efficient technologies and renewable energy projects.

risks.risk: Physical climate risk to manufacturing and logistics continuity
risks.note: BRSR material issue 2, Climate Change Adaptation, flagged as a Risk: extreme weather events, changing climatic conditions and resource constraints may disrupt manufacturing operations, logistics and the availability of critical inputs, with financial impact from production downtime, logistics and raw-material supply disruption and reduced manufacturing capacity utilisation.

risks.risk: Waste and circularity compliance alongside shifting product-efficiency regulation
risks.note: BRSR material issue 4, Waste Management and Circularity, warns that inadequate management of metal scrap, plastic waste, packaging waste and other industrial solid waste may result in regulatory non-compliance, increased disposal costs and environmental impacts; the MD&A separately notes enhanced BEE energy-efficiency standards and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations reshaping product design and reverse-logistics requirements across the industry.

one-line thesis: EPACK delivered resilient Q3 growth (13.5% YoY) with margin expansion (7.41%) driven by a 74% surge in LDA and 61% in Components, successfully offsetting a marginal RAC decline. The strategic pivot away from RAC dependency (now ~57-60%) toward higher-margin SDA, LDA, and components is de-risking the model ahead of a projected 15-20% industry recovery in CY26 driven by new BEE norms.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 427.8 Cr (+13.5% YoY); EBITDA: INR 31.7 Cr (+31.5% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 7.41% (+102 bps YoY); PAT: INR 2.6 Cr (+4% YoY, margin contracted 5 bps due to higher depreciation/finance costs); Order Book: Robust, aligned with brand plans for 15-20% growth over FY25; Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified, but finance costs cited as headwind to PAT; One-offs: Higher depreciation from INR 218 Cr capex in 9M FY26 impacting net profit despite operating leverage.
guidance: Revenue Growth: AC segment 25-30% CAGR to 2030; Industry AC growth 15-20% in CY26; Margin: Targeting 7.5-8% EBITDA medium-term; Order Inflow: Strong RFQs for new BEE-rated products; Capex: INR 450 Cr planned over 12-18 months (INR 218 Cr spent in 9M FY26, INR 225 Cr remaining).
order book & pipeline: Described as 'very robust' with brands planning 15-20% growth over FY25 numbers; Current production ramping for new BEE-rated units; Inventory liquidation of old-rated stock (4-4.5 Mn units in channel) expected to normalize by end-Q4 FY26, triggering fresh manufacturing orders.
segment / subsidiary detail: RAC: Marginal 1% YoY decline (industry degrowth); SDA: +30% YoY (Air fryers, nutri blenders); LDA: +74% YoY (Washing machines, coolers); Components: +61% YoY (PCBs, copper parts, plastic molding for AC, meters, coolers). RAC contribution ~57-60%, targeting 55% by FY28/29.
growth verticals / optionality: Washing machine vertical (fully auto top/front load) ramping with new MNC customers; Hisense JV commencing production Q4 FY26 (RAC, then WM/TV); Component segment expanding beyond AC to electrical meters and audio; New SDA launches (vacuum cleaners, tower fans) in Q4 FY26.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margins: RAC ~14-15%; SDA/LDA/Components ~16-18%. Cost Headwinds: 8-10% price hike required (50% BEE re-rating, 50% commodity lag from Oct-Dec); Commodity pass-through mechanism protects absolute margins but may compress % margins if base prices rise significantly.
capex / expansion: INR 218 Cr incurred in 9M FY26 (Q1: 45, Q2: 130, Q3: 45); Focus on washing machine lines, Sricity component plant, Hisense JV, and Bhiwadi greenfield; Remaining INR 225 Cr to be deployed over next 6-9 months.
capital allocation: Diligent product-wise ROI monitoring before launch; Funding multi-category expansion while protecting returns; Strategic JV with Hisense to share capex burden for new facilities.
risks & watch-items: Commodity price volatility (copper, aluminum) exceeding pass-through capabilities; Seasonal demand mismatch for AC; High channel inventory (4-4.5 Mn units) delaying order normalization; Regulatory costs (E-waste, BEE norms) squeezing brand budgets.
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'resilience' despite external headwinds; Clear strategic shift from volume-only RAC to balanced high-margin mix; Transparent on cost pass-through mechanics.
non-obvious takeaways: Trade payable days dropped drastically in Q3 due to consumption of existing inventory without new procurement (seasonal lull); Normalized payable days are 90-100. Management explicitly states top-2 customer concentration (now 35-40%) is 'ideal' and will not be reduced further, shifting focus to wallet-share expansion via cross-selling rather than dilution.

business_model.body: EPACK Durable designs and manufactures room air conditioners (split indoor units, outdoor units and window air conditioners), large and small domestic appliances and critical components for prominent Indian and global consumer-appliance brands, providing end-to-end product solutions from design and development through manufacturing and supply chain management. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Household RAC penetration in India remains at around 8-10%, significantly below other Asian markets, giving substantial headroom for growth alongside rising temperatures, frequent heatwaves and increasing affordability.
- India's air conditioning market, valued at approximately USD 4.46 billion in 2025, is projected to grow at a CAGR of 14.53% through 2034, underscoring the opportunity for organised manufacturers.
- India's consumer durables market is projected to reach approximately Rs 5.39 lakh crore by FY 2029-30, registering a CAGR of around 14%.
- Management expects improved customer demand conditions and gradual normalisation in industry inventory levels, supported by favourable domestic factors and supportive policy measures.
- Non-RAC segments are the growth engine: SDA and LDA grew on healthy order inflows from existing and newly launched products, while enhanced localisation and deeper customer integration drove strong growth in the Components division.
- FY 2025-26 was a challenging year for the RAC industry - unseasonal weather, inventory correction across channels and revised BEE norms hit industry demand and profitability, a transition-year effect rather than a structural one in management's framing.
- Margin narrative: EBITDA margin of 6.01% absorbed a one-time reversal of previously recognised PLI income accrued April to December 2025, partly mitigated by RIPS 2024 incentive income recognised in Q4, of which part related to earlier periods.
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP is projected to grow between 6.8% and 7.2% in FY 2026-27, with consumer demand expected to remain resilient on rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and premiumisation.
- Structural demand shifts: premiumisation, energy efficiency and BEE labelling, AI/IoT-enabled smart appliances, Tier II and Tier III penetration, omnichannel and e-commerce expansion, and EPR-driven circularity.
- Diversification of global supply chains is expected to create opportunities for India to strengthen its position as a manufacturing and export hub for consumer durables and electronics.
- SDA and LDA growth was driven by healthy order inflows from both existing and newly launched products (no quantified order book disclosed).
- FY 2026-27 scale-up of SDA and LDA is to be supported by new product development, deeper customer engagement and a healthy order pipeline.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margins: RAC ~14-15%; SDA/LDA/Components ~16-18%. Cost Headwinds: 8-10% price hike required (50% BEE re-rating, 50% commodity lag from Oct-Dec); Commodity pass-through mechanism protects absolute margins but may compress % margins if base prices rise significantly.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Diligent product-wise ROI monitoring before launch; Funding multi-category expansion while protecting returns; Strategic JV with Hisense to share capex burden for new facilities.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was an expansion year: the Company invested a total CAPEX of Rs 2,971 million directed at localisation, backward integration of component capabilities and future capacity expansion, against a Strategic CAPEX Roadmap with a total investment outlay of Rs 4,700 million spread across the Dehradun, Bhiwadi and Sri City facilities of EPACK Durable and the EMTPL facility at Sri City. Operations commenced under the Hisense partnership through wholly-owned subsidiary EPACK Manufacturing Technologies Private Limited (EMTPL) at Sri City in Q4 FY 2025-26, and EMTPL is expected to gradually contribute to revenues, product mix and future growth as operations scale over the coming quarters. Targeted capital expenditure continues to be deployed to ramp up capacity at newer facilities like Sri City and to support new product lines such as washing machines, while component capability is being widened including a joint venture to produce BLDC motors. Going forward, management says the focus remains on disciplined scale-up and optimising capacity utilisation to realise the full potential of these investments; Phase-2 investment opportunities under RIPS 2024 at Bhiwadi are under evaluation with a focus on advanced RAC components, electronics manufacturing, localisation and export-oriented production. Alongside plant capex, an aggregate solar power generation capacity of 2,332 kW has been installed across all manufacturing units and in-house nitrogen generation plants were established at the Sri City, Bhiwadi and Dehradun facilities.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'resilience' despite external headwinds; Clear strategic shift from volume-only RAC to balanced high-margin mix; Transparent on cost pass-through mechanics.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Highest level of backward integration for RACs at a single location in India - stated as a key competitive advantage enabling superior cost management, efficient inventory control and reduced exposure to supply chain volatility, particularly from imports
- Second-largest RAC ODM in India by volume of units manufactured, with a legacy spanning over two decades as a manufacturing partner to prominent Indian and global brands
- In-house manufacture of critical components - heat exchangers, PCBAs, copper tubing, cross flow fans, universal motors, induction coils, sheet metal and injection-moulded parts - for both captive consumption and external supply
- Dedicated R&D centres at Bhiwadi, Dehradun and Sri City with advanced testing and design facilities including NABL-accredited labs
- Multi-site manufacturing footprint across Dehradun, Bhiwadi and Sri City facilitating efficient pan-India logistics and proximity to key customer markets
- Quality system spanning Incoming (IQC), Line (LQC) and Outgoing (OQC) quality control plus early-life and reliability testing, backed by ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certification
- Access to government incentive schemes - PLI for White Goods, RIPS 2024 in Rajasthan with Large Category status under the ESDM thrust sector, and ECMS under MeitY
- SAP S/4 HANA implemented to optimise operations and guarantee accurate record maintenance

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Commodity price volatility (copper, aluminum) exceeding pass-through capabilities; Seasonal demand mismatch for AC; High channel inventory (4-4.5 Mn units) delaying order normalization; Regulatory costs (E-waste, BEE norms) squeezing brand budgets.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Trade payable days dropped drastically in Q3 due to consumption of existing inventory without new procurement (seasonal lull); Normalized payable days are 90-100. Management explicitly states top-2 customer concentration (now 35-40%) is 'ideal' and will not be reduced further, shifting focus to wallet-share expansion via cross-selling rather than dilution.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversify beyond the seasonal RAC business by scaling the Small Domestic Appliances, Large Domestic Appliances and Components verticals - FY 2026-27 focus is on strengthening the core RAC business while accelerating scale-up of SDA and LDA through new product development, deeper customer engagement and a healthy order pipeline.
- Deepen and broaden the customer base: deeper penetration across key customer accounts plus new relationships took the customer base from 55 in FY 2024-25 to 72 in FY 2025-26, with continued expansion of market presence targeted.
- Increase localisation and backward …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [PLI] The Company has not accrued any PLI income during Q1 FY27, whereas it had accrued PLI income of Rs 133 Mn during Q1 FY26 — the deck footnotes this against its revenue, EBITDA and PBT figures.
- [JV] EPAVO (Bhiwadi) is a JV within the five-plant footprint; the consolidated share of JV loss widened each year — Rs (8) Mn FY23, Rs (15) Mn FY24, Rs (30) Mn FY25, Rs (65) Mn FY26.
- [Margin narrative] The deck frames the current margin pressure as "a sector-wide theme this quarter" and sets the near-term priority as "translating record scale into profitability".
- [Market] Stock data as on 30 June 2026: CMP Rs 230.81, 52-week high/low Rs 414.7 / 196.0, market cap Rs 22,210 Mn, 96 Mn shares outstanding, average volume 1,841k; the deck says the stock "underperformed the Sensex over FY26, tracking the earnings pressure across the RAC sector - a re-rating opportunity if margins and returns recover."

one-line thesis: EPACK delivered resilient Q3 growth (13.5% YoY) with margin expansion (7.41%) driven by a 74% surge in LDA and 61% in Components, successfully offsetting a marginal RAC decline. The strategic pivot away from RAC dependency (now ~57-60%) toward higher-margin SDA, LDA, and components is de-risking the model ahead of a projected 15-20% industry recovery in CY26 driven by new BEE norms.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 427.8 Cr (+13.5% YoY); EBITDA: INR 31.7 Cr (+31.5% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 7.41% (+102 bps YoY); PAT: INR 2.6 Cr (+4% YoY, margin contracted 5 bps due to higher depreciation/finance costs); Order Book: Robust, aligned with brand plans for 15-20% growth over FY25; Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified, but finance costs cited as headwind to PAT; One-offs: Higher depreciation from INR 218 Cr capex in 9M FY26 impacting net profit despite operating leverage.
guidance: Revenue Growth: AC segment 25-30% CAGR to 2030; Industry AC growth 15-20% in CY26; Margin: Targeting 7.5-8% EBITDA medium-term; Order Inflow: Strong RFQs for new BEE-rated products; Capex: INR 450 Cr planned over 12-18 months (INR 218 Cr spent in 9M FY26, INR 225 Cr remaining).
order book & pipeline: Described as 'very robust' with brands planning 15-20% growth over FY25 numbers; Current production ramping for new BEE-rated units; Inventory liquidation of old-rated stock (4-4.5 Mn units in channel) expected to normalize by end-Q4 FY26, triggering fresh manufacturing orders.
segment / subsidiary detail: RAC: Marginal 1% YoY decline (industry degrowth); SDA: +30% YoY (Air fryers, nutri blenders); LDA: +74% YoY (Washing machines, coolers); Components: +61% YoY (PCBs, copper parts, plastic molding for AC, meters, coolers). RAC contribution ~57-60%, targeting 55% by FY28/29.
growth verticals / optionality: Washing machine vertical (fully auto top/front load) ramping with new MNC customers; Hisense JV commencing production Q4 FY26 (RAC, then WM/TV); Component segment expanding beyond AC to electrical meters and audio; New SDA launches (vacuum cleaners, tower fans) in Q4 FY26.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margins: RAC ~14-15%; SDA/LDA/Components ~16-18%. Cost Headwinds: 8-10% price hike required (50% BEE re-rating, 50% commodity lag from Oct-Dec); Commodity pass-through mechanism protects absolute margins but may compress % margins if base prices rise significantly.
capex / expansion: INR 218 Cr incurred in 9M FY26 (Q1: 45, Q2: 130, Q3: 45); Focus on washing machine lines, Sricity component plant, Hisense JV, and Bhiwadi greenfield; Remaining INR 225 Cr to be deployed over next 6-9 months.
capital allocation: Diligent product-wise ROI monitoring before launch; Funding multi-category expansion while protecting returns; Strategic JV with Hisense to share capex burden for new facilities.
